def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion:
## Definition

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].
def-qc-trace-norm:
## Definition

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces. Its singular values are the eigenvalues of
$|A|:=\sqrt{A^*A}:H\to H$, counted with multiplicity, as defined in
[[def-singular-values-of-an-endomorphism]]. Define the **trace norm**, or
Schatten-$1$ norm, by

$$\|A\|_1:=\sum_{j<\dim H}s_j(A).$$

The sum includes zero singular values and is $0$ when $H$ is the zero space.
For this definition, $A$ may be rectangular; the singular values are those of
$|A|$ on the domain $H$. The spectral trace formula is proved in
[[thm-qc-trace-norm-spectral-formula]].
thm-qc-dirac-adjoint-amplitude-translati:
## Statement

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $T:H\to K$
be linear, and let $x\in K$, $y\in H$. With the Dirac conversion
[[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]],

$$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D:=\langle x|Ty\rangle_D =\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}} =\langle y,T^*x\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}} =\langle T^*x|y\rangle_D.$$
thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identit:
## Statement

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with ordered
orthonormal bases $E=(e_j)_{j<n}$ and $F=(f_i)_{i<m}$. Let $T:H\to K$ be
linear ([[def-linear-map]]), and write $T_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry of its
matrix in these bases.
Then, for every $z\in H$,

$$Tz=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}\langle z,e_j\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}f_i, \qquad T=\sum_{j<n}\sum_{i<m}T_{ij}|f_i\rangle\langle e_j|.$$

For $x\in K$ and $y\in H$, the rank-one map $|x\rangle\langle y|$ has
coordinate matrix $[x]_F[y]_E^\dagger$, where $M^\dagger=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$.
Its amplitude satisfies
$\langle x|T|y\rangle_D=\langle Ty,x\rangle_{K,\mathrm{root}}$.
All sums are empty when an index dimension is zero, and the identities include
those cases.
thm-qc-trace-norm-duality-and-norm-prope:
## Statement

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. Then

$$\|A\|_1=\max\{\,|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|: B:H\to K\text{ linear and }\|B\|_\infty\le1\,\}.$$

Consequently, on the vector space of linear maps $H\to K$, the trace norm is
nonnegative, absolutely homogeneous, definite, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.
thm-qc-trace-norm-rank-one-formula:
## Statement

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, $x\in K$,
$y\in H$, and $|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K$ the rank-one linear map
([[def-linear-map]]) from [[def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion]]. Then

$$\big\||x\rangle\langle y|\big\|_1=\|x\|\,\|y\|.$$
thm-qc-trace-norm-spectral-formula:
## Statement

For every linear map $A:H\to K$ ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces,

$$\|A\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H\!\left(\sqrt{A^*A}\right).$$

Here $A^*A$ and its non-negative square root are endomorphisms of the domain
$H$; the trace is taken on $H$.
thm-qc-trace-norm-unitary-invariance-and:
## Statement

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. If $U:K\to K$ and $V:H\to H$ are unitary, then
$\|UAV\|_1=\|A\|_1$. If $P:H\to H$ is non-negative (positive semidefinite),
then

$$\|P\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H(P).$$

Here non-negative means self-adjoint with
$\langle Pv,v\rangle\ge0$ for all $v$, as in
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]].
prop-qc-trace-holder-inequality:
## Statement

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$ and compatible
linear maps $A,B:H\to K$ ([[def-linear-map]]), the composite $B^*A$ is an
endomorphism of $H$ and

$$|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|\le\|A\|_1\,\|B\|_\infty.$$
thm-qc-hermitian-trace-norm-positive-neg:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$X:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$ be self-adjoint. There are non-negative
endomorphisms $X_+,X_-$ such that

$$X=X_+-X_-,\qquad \langle X_+u,X_-v\rangle=0\quad(u,v\in\mathcal H),$$

and

$$\|X\|_1=\operatorname{tr}(X_+)+\operatorname{tr}(X_-).$$

If $\operatorname{tr}(X)=0$, then
$\|X\|_1=2\operatorname{tr}(X_+)=2\operatorname{tr}(X_-)$. 

The trace norm is the finite singular-value norm from
[[def-qc-trace-norm]].
